mainTopic: Setting bones and treating dislocations on שבת; the end of פרק חבית; borrowing on שבת without loan wording
overview: The גמרא rules like שמואל that one may set a broken bone on שבת, even though our משנה says אין מחזירין את השבר. A story shows רב יהודה having רבה בר בר חנה dragged to his lecture, only to learn this very ruling from him. Next, רב אויא asks רב יוסף about positioning his dislocated hand. רב יוסף says the משנה forbids treating a dislocated limb. רב יוסף answers רב אויא's challenge from שמואל's ruling by saying that ruling applies only where it was stated. After the הדרן for פרק חבית, a new chapter opens with a משנה: one may borrow wine, oil, or loaves on שבת, and may leave a cloak as security, but may not say "הלויני". אביי explains that loan wording leads the lender to write, and that on שבת the special wording keeps people aware of the day. Finally, אביי explains why women do not change how they draw water on יום טוב: any change would only add effort.

steps.title: The ruling: one may set a broken bone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that it is permitted to set a broken bone on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: one may set a broken bone back in place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling: setting a broken bone on שבת is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said אין מחזירין את השבר, meaning one may not set a break. The גמרא rules the opposite, following שמואל's version as reported by רב חנא בגדתאה. Everything that follows builds on this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law; the final ruling

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה: a broken bone may be set on שבת, even though the plain משנה seems to forbid it.

phrases.english: The halacha is: one may reset a break.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the discussion from the previous daf about שמואל's version of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setting a broken bone on שבת is permitted.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה is dragged to רב יהודה's lecture
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה visits פומבדיתא and skips רב יהודה's lecture, so רב יהודה has his attendant bring him by force.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה came to פומבדיתא and did not attend רב יהודה's lecture. רב יהודה sent אדא, his attendant, and told him: Go drag him here. He went and dragged him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that supports the ruling just stated. This step sets the scene for the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A visiting scholar was expected to attend the local רב's lecture. רב יהודה took the absence seriously and had רבה בר בר חנה brought by force. The story's point becomes clear in the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אִיקְּלַע לְפוּמְבְּדִיתָא,
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana happened to come to Pumbedita,
and he did not enter Rav Yehuda's lecture.
He sent Adda the attendant for him,
and said to him: Go drag him.
He went and dragged him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אִיקְּלַע לְפוּמְבְּדִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that will show where the ruling of step 1 came from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: רבה בר בר חנה is brought to רב יהודה's lecture.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה corrects the lecture with שמואל's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה is teaching that one may not set a break, and רבה בר בר חנה quotes שמואל saying one may.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came and found רב יהודה teaching: One may not set a break. He said to him: This is what רב חנא בגדתאה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is that one may set a break.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה challenges רב יהודה's teaching with a ruling from שמואל that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה was teaching the plain wording of the משנה. רבה בר בר חנה brings a tradition that שמואל ruled to permit it, so the lecture needs correcting.

keyTerms.meaning: רב חנא of Baghdad, who transmitted שמואל's ruling

phrases.english: He came and found him expounding:
One may not reset a break.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּגְדָּתָאָה
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rav Ḥana of Baghdad said
that Shmuel said:
The halacha is: one may reset a break.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּגְדָּתָאָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Inside the story, the dragged guest corrects the lecture.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's teaching that one may not set a break
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A tradition from שמואל rules the opposite, so the halacha follows that ruling.

steps.title: רב יהודה: I was right to bring you
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה admits he had not heard this ruling and says that is why bringing רבה בר בר חנה was justified.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רב חנא is one of ours, and שמואל is one of ours, yet I never heard this. Wasn't I right to drag you here?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה accepts the correction and closes the story with a witty point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה accepts the ruling of שמואל, his own teacher, even though he had not heard it before. The story ends with the הלכה confirmed: one may set a break. Bringing the guest turned out to be worthwhile.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows שמואל: one may set a broken bone on שבת, and even רב יהודה accepted this.

phrases.english: He said to him: Ḥana is ours,
and Shmuel is ours,
and I did not hear it;
did I not rightfully drag you?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יהודה accepts the correction from step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ruling of שמואל is accepted: one may set a broken bone on שבת.

steps.title: רב אויא asks about positioning his dislocated hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה on dislocated limbs. רב אויא's hand slips out of place, and he asks רב יוסף which hand positions are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: One whose hand was dislocated, etc. רב אויא was sitting before רב יוסף, and his hand became dislocated. He asked: What about this position? Forbidden. And what about this one? He said: Forbidden. Meanwhile his hand healed by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about a dislocated limb, and tells a story about a practical question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אויא wanted to know which hand positions count as forbidden healing (רפואה) on שבת. רב יוסף forbade each one. Meanwhile the hand went back into place by itself, which sets up the next exchange.

phrases.english: One whose hand was dislocated, etc.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַוְיָא הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף,
phrases.english: Rav Avya was sitting before Rav Yosef,
and his hand became dislocated.
He said to him: What about this? It is prohibited.
And what about this? He said to him: It is prohibited.
In the meantime, his hand healed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה, about dislocated limbs.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which positions of a dislocated hand are allowed on שבת and which count as forbidden healing?

steps.title: רב יוסף: the משנה already answers this
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks why there was any doubt and cites the משנה, which forbids treating a dislocated limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is your question? We learned: One whose hand or foot was dislocated may not shake it vigorously in cold water, but he may wash normally, and if it heals, it heals.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings proof from the משנה that the forbidden answers were obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly forbids active treatment of a dislocated limb. Normal washing is allowed, and any healing that happens is incidental. So רב יוסף sees no room for a question.

phrases.english: He said to him: What is your question?

phrases.aramaic: הָא תְּנַן: מִי שֶׁנִּפְרְקָה יָדוֹ אוֹ רַגְלוֹ —
phrases.english: We learned: One whose hand or foot was dislocated
may not shake them vigorously in cold water,
but he may wash in his usual way,
and if it heals, it heals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Justifies the forbidden answers given in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: Treating a dislocated limb on שבת is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: מי שנפרקה ידו או רגלו לא יטרפם בצונן.

steps.title: רב אויא: the משנה on breaks was also overridden
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא argues that the משנה alone is not decisive, because שמואל permitted setting a break against the משנה's wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Didn't we also learn: One may not set a break? Yet רב חנא בגדתאה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is that one may set a break!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא challenges רב יוסף's proof by showing that a nearby rule in the same משנה was not followed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמואל's ruling overrode the משנה on broken bones, maybe the rule on dislocations is also not the final הלכה. That is why רב אויא felt he had a real question.

phrases.english: He said to him: But didn't we learn:
"One may not reset a break,"

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּגְדָּתָאָהּ אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: and Rav Ḥana of Baghdad said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is: one may reset a break!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא תְּנַן: אֵין מַחֲזִירִין אֶת הַשֶּׁבֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's proof from the משנה in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's assumption that the משנה's rule on dislocations is the final הלכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A neighboring rule in the same משנה was overridden by שמואל, so perhaps the dislocation rule was overridden too.

steps.title: רב יוסף: each ruling stands on its own
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the rulings are not one woven piece. Where an exception was stated it applies, and where it was not stated it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Were they all woven in a single weave? Where it was said, it was said. Where it was not said, it was not said.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the challenge: שמואל's exception for broken bones does not carry over to dislocations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Overriding one clause of a משנה does not cancel the other clauses. שמואל spoke only about setting breaks, so the משנה's ban on treating a dislocated limb still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: A broken bone may be set on שבת, following שמואל. A dislocated limb may not be actively treated, following the משנה. An exception applies only where it was stated.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that because שמואל overrode one line of the משנה, every nearby line is also overridden. Each ruling stands on its own.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כּוּלְּהוּ בַּחֲדָא מְחִיתָא מְחִיתִּנְהוּ?!
phrases.english: He said to him: Were they all woven in a single weave?!
Where it was stated, it was stated;
where it was not stated, it was not stated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אויא's challenge from step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's permission to set breaks might mean the whole משנה, including dislocations, is not the הלכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל's ruling covers only broken bones. The ban on treating dislocations stays in force.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק חבית
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the chapter פרק חבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק חבית.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line said at the end of a chapter. It closes פרק חבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן marks the end of the chapter and expresses the wish to return to it and learn it again. The next chapter begins after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (chapter-closing formula)
Barrel; the name of this chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, Chapter "Chavit".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion.

steps.title: New chapter: borrowing on שבת without saying 'loan me'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה permits borrowing wine, oil, or loaves from a friend on שבת, as long as the borrower avoids the word "הלוויני". If the lender does not trust him, he leaves his cloak as security and they settle up after שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may borrow jugs of wine and jugs of oil from his friend on שבת, as long as he does not say "loan me." A woman may likewise borrow loaves from her friend. If the lender does not trust the borrower, the borrower leaves his cloak with him, and they settle the account after שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה. It teaches how a person may borrow food items on שבת without it looking like a weekday business loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission depends on the wording. "Borrow" language is allowed, but "loan me" (הלוויני) is not. The cloak works as security without any writing or formal deal on שבת, and the actual accounting waits until after שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of the משנה text.
Borrows. It is also the name of this new chapter.
"Loan me." This is the forbidden loan wording on שבת.
His cloak, left with the lender as security.
An account, meaning settling up what is owed.

steps.confusionAlert: Leaving the cloak is not a sale and not a written deal. It is just security left in the lender's hands, so nothing businesslike happens on שבת itself.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A person may borrow from his friend
jugs of wine and jugs of oil,
provided that he does not say to him "loan me."
And likewise a woman may borrow loaves from her friend.
And if the lender does not trust him,
the borrower leaves his cloak with him,
and settles the account with him after Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the closing formula of פרק חבית in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Borrowing on שבת is permitted with borrow language but not with "loan me." Security may be left, and the accounting happens after שבת.

steps.title: Same method for the קרבן פסח when ערב פסח falls on שבת
steps.stepSummary: When ערב פסח in Jerusalem falls on שבת, a person may leave his cloak with the seller, take his קרבן פסח, and settle up after יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Likewise, when ערב פסח in Jerusalem falls on שבת, a person leaves his cloak with the owner, takes his קרבן פסח lamb, and settles the account after יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same cloak-as-security method to a real-life case: getting a קרבן פסח on a שבת that is ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lamb cannot be bought normally on שבת, but the קרבן פסח must still be brought that day. The cloak guarantees payment without any purchase on שבת, and payment waits until after יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The day before פסח, when the קרבן פסח is brought.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's core idea is to get what you need on שבת without loan wording and without business. Leave security, and pay later.

phrases.english: And likewise, on Erev Pesach in Jerusalem
that happens to fall on Shabbat,
he leaves his cloak with him,
and takes his Pesach offering,

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹשֶׂה עִמּוֹ חֶשְׁבּוֹן לְאַחַר יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: and settles the account with him after the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן עֶרֶב פֶּסַח בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the cloak-security method of step 10 to the case of the קרבן פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a שבת that is ערב פסח, one may take the קרבן פסח by leaving security and paying after יום טוב.

steps.title: What is the difference between 'let me borrow' and 'loan me'?
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנן asks אביי why the משנה allows "השאילני" but forbids "הלוויני".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב חנן said to אביי: What is different about "let me borrow," and what is different about "loan me"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רבא בר רב חנן asks why the משנה cares about which word the borrower uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both words describe getting something now and paying it back later. So the משנה's distinction needs a reason. The question asks for that reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה.
"Let me borrow." This is the permitted wording.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rava bar Rav Ḥanan said to Abaye:
What is different about "let me borrow,"
and what is different about "loan me"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הַשְׁאִילֵנִי, וּמַאי שְׁנָא הַלְוֵינִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the wording distinction in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason why "loan me" is forbidden on שבת while "let me borrow" is permitted.

steps.title: Loan language leads people to write it down
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that a borrowing does not lead the lender to write it down, but a loan does. Writing is forbidden on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: With "let me borrow," the lender will not come to write it down. With "loan me," he will come to write it down.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the reason for the משנה's rule. The concern is that the lender will write the loan down, which is forbidden on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A borrowed item is returned as the same object soon, so nobody bothers writing a record. A loan is longer and the item is replaced rather than returned, so lenders tend to record it. Since writing (כתיבה) is a forbidden מלאכה on שבת, the חכמים banned the loan wording.

keyTerms.meaning: He will come to write. This is the feared outcome.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַשְׁאִילֵנִי — לָא אָתֵי לְמִיכְתַּב,
phrases.english: He said to him: With "let me borrow," he will not come to write,
with "loan me," he will come to write.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַשְׁאִילֵנִי לָא אָתֵי לְמִיכְתַּב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Loan wording tends to lead to writing the loan down, which is forbidden on שבת. Borrow wording does not.

steps.title: But people mix up the two words on weekdays
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנן challenges אביי: on weekdays people say "השאילני" when they mean a loan, and lenders still write it down. So the same should happen on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since on weekdays a person sometimes means to say "loan me" and says "let me borrow" instead, and the lender does not mind and comes to write it down, then on שבת he will also come to write it down!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר רב חנן attacks אביי's answer. He argues that the word itself does not really control whether people write.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people use the two words loosely on weekdays, and lenders write in both cases, then "let me borrow" can also lead to writing. That would make the משנה's distinction pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: He is not particular. He does not mind the wording.

phrases.english: But since on a weekday,
sometimes he means to say to him "loan me"
and he says to him "let me borrow,"
and the lender is not particular about it, and comes to write,
on Shabbat too he will come to write!

steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that "let me borrow" does not lead to writing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Weekday speech shows the words are used interchangeably and loans get written either way. So the wording cannot prevent writing on שבת.

steps.title: On Shabbat the difference stands out, so no one will write
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that on weekdays nobody cares about the wording. On שבת, because only "השאילני" was permitted, the distinction is noticed, and that awareness prevents writing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: On a weekday, when it makes no difference whether he says "loan me" or "let me borrow," we are not particular about it, and he comes to write. On שבת, since only "let me borrow" was permitted by the חכמים and "loan me" was not permitted, the matter is noticeable, and he will not come to write.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his answer. He explains that the special שבת rule itself changes how people think.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Weekday carelessness happens because nothing depends on the wording. On שבת both sides must pay attention to which word is allowed. That attention reminds them it is שבת, so they will not write.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter is noticeable. It stands out.

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the word magically stops writing. He is saying the act of watching your words on שבת keeps you aware that it is שבת.

phrases.english: He said to him: On a weekday,
where it makes no difference whether he says "loan me"
or whether he says "let me borrow,"
we are not particular about it, so he comes to write.

phrases.aramaic: בְּשַׁבָּת כֵּיוָן דְּ״הַשְׁאִילֵנִי״ הוּא דְּשָׁרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: On Shabbat, since it is only "let me borrow" that the Sages permitted,
and "loan me" they did not permit,
the matter is noticeable, and he will not come to write.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשַׁבָּת כֵּיוָן דְּ״הַשְׁאִילֵנִי״ הוּא דְּשָׁרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes weekday from שבת: the שבת rule creates awareness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Weekday interchangeability means the wording makes no difference on שבת either.
steps.terutzMaskana: On שבת the permitted wording is noticed, and that awareness prevents writing.
steps.whatToRemember: Loan wording is banned on שבת because it leads to writing. Sticking to borrow wording keeps both people aware that it is שבת.

steps.title: Why don't women change how they draw water on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנן notes the rule that on יום טוב we change our weekday way of doing things whenever possible. He asks why women drawing water do not change theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב חנן said to אביי: Since the חכמים said that for all matters of יום טוב we change from the weekday way as much as possible, why do these women who fill their pitchers with water not change how they do it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר רב חנן raises a new question about יום טוב. It points to an everyday practice that seems to go against a known rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says to make יום טוב activities look different from weekdays wherever possible. Yet women draw water exactly as they do on weekdays. This looks like a gap between the rule and common practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, after all. It introduces an accepted premise.
We make a change from the usual way.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Ḥanan said to Abaye:
Now, since the Sages said:
for all matters of a Festival,
as much as it is possible to change, we change,
these women who fill their pitchers with water,
what is the reason they do not change?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new exchange between the same two אמוראים, on the topic of changing behavior on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The common practice of women drawing water on יום טוב in the normal way.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule requires a change wherever possible, so unchanged water-drawing seems to break it.

steps.title: Any change would only make the work harder
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that no useful change is possible. A smaller pitcher means more walking, and a larger pitcher means a heavier load.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is not possible. How would they do it? If those who usually fill a large pitcher filled a small one, they would add to their walking. If those who usually fill a small pitcher filled a large one, they would add to their load.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains that the rule only applies where a change is possible. Here every change just adds effort.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says "as much as possible," and changing the way water is drawn only makes יום טוב harder. So this is an exception in how the rule is carried out. The rule itself still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The יום טוב rule to change one's usual way applies only when a change is practical. If it just adds work, no change is required.

phrases.english: Because it is not possible:
How would they do it?

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָלְיָין בְּחַצְבָּא רַבָּא, לִימְלוֹ בְּחַצְבָּא זוּטָא —
phrases.english: Those who fill with a large pitcher should fill with a small pitcher?
Then they add to their walking.

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָלְיָין בְּחַצְבָּא זוּטָא, לִימְלוֹ בְּחַצְבָּא רַבָּא —
phrases.english: Those who fill with a small pitcher should fill with a large pitcher?
Then they add to the load.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule's application to cases where a change is practical.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every יום טוב activity must be done differently from weekdays.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where every change only adds effort, no change is required.
